description: Recruiter-style questions over the synthetic resume corpus (sample_resumes/*.txt and sample_resumes/varied/*). A label is a chunk that directly evidences the answer, identified by resume file, section and a quote the chunk must contain. Labels are a DRAFT pending human review; nothing is measured until they are approved.

questions.question: Who has run FastAPI services in production?
questions.rationale: Rachel migrated to FastAPI microservices 'running in production'; Omar deployed FastAPI model services on Cloud Run. Distractor: Aarav (v01) built a FastAPI API for coursework that was explicitly 'Not deployed', and skills lists that only name FastAPI are not evidence of production use.

questions.question: Which candidates have built retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems?
questions.rationale: All three describe building a RAG system (Aarav's as a student project, which still counts as having built one). Javier (resume_10) 'connected retrieval systems to user products', which is adjacent but not RAG, so it is not labelled.

questions.question: Who has hands-on Kafka experience?
questions.rationale: Rachel designed a Kafka backbone in production; Diego built a Kafka producer/consumer demo. Both are hands-on; the recruiter can weigh depth from the cited text.

questions.question: Find candidates with a Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) certification.
questions.rationale: Only Tom holds the CKA. His resume has no headings, so the answer is in an unlabelled chunk: a deliberate hard case.

questions.question: Who has security certifications such as OSCP or CISSP?
questions.rationale: Fatima's certifications section lists both. Keyword-heavy question, should favour BM25.

questions.question: Which candidates have managed or mentored engineers?
questions.rationale: Rachel mentored engineers; Elena manages two teams. Elena's skills chunk mentions 'mentoring' as a word but is not evidence of having done it, so it is not labelled.

questions.question: Who has worked with Terraform?
questions.rationale: Rachel lists Terraform in skills (her experience section does not mention it); Tom manages clusters with Terraform. A skills list counts here because the question asks about any Terraform work, not production depth.

questions.question: Find freshers who built a chatbot project.
questions.rationale: Aarav is a fresher (graduating 2026) with a campus chatbot project. No other fresher built a chatbot.

questions.question: Who knows React and TypeScript?

relevant.contains: checkout frontend in React and TypeScript

questions.rationale: Liam and Elena both evidence React and TypeScript in a project/experience chunk and in skills; all four chunks answer the question.

questions.question: Who has built Android apps?

relevant.contains: Kotlin and Jetpack Compose banking app

questions.rationale: Kwame shipped an Android banking app. His resume uses inline headings ('Experience: ...'), a format test.

questions.question: Which candidate has compressed large language models to run on a laptop?
questions.rationale: Paraphrase test: 'compressed ... to run on a laptop' vs 'Quantized ... for laptop inference'. Should favour vector search.

questions.question: Who has published research papers?
questions.rationale: Only Chen Wei lists publications. Emma (resume_09) 'benchmarked NLP systems' but lists no publications.

questions.question: Who has built data pipelines with Airflow or dbt?
questions.rationale: Diego built an Airflow + dbt pipeline; Priya automated reporting with dbt. Priya's two-column layout leaves everything in one unlabelled chunk: a format hard case.

questions.question: Who has built dashboards in Power BI?
questions.rationale: Hannah built Power BI dashboards. Priya built dashboards in Looker, not Power BI, so she is not labelled.

questions.question: Find a candidate who moved into tech from teaching.
questions.rationale: Hannah was a teacher for 6 years before data analysis. Sara (v02) was a teaching assistant during her degree, which is not a career change.

questions.question: Who has experience with vector databases or semantic search?
questions.rationale: Sophia built semantic search and lists vector databases; Javier lists vector databases; Omar used pgvector in a RAG system. Aarav (v01) used FAISS, a vector index library, in a project; arguably relevant, left unlabelled for the reviewer to decide.

questions.question: Who has evaluated an LLM system with a golden dataset?
questions.rationale: Omar ran offline evaluation with RAGAS and a golden set. Michael and Emma mention 'evaluation' generally but not a golden dataset.

questions.question: Which candidates have used MLflow?
questions.rationale: Exact keyword in two skills lists; a pure keyword question.

questions.question: Which candidates hold a PhD?
questions.rationale: Only Chen Wei. Tests matching 'PhD' against 'Ph.D.'.

questions.question: Who has fine-tuned transformer models?
questions.rationale: Michael built fine-tuning pipelines, Lina's summary states fine-tuning experience, Sara fine-tuned DistilBERT. Ananya and Emma do not mention fine-tuning.

questions.question: Who made a slow nightly batch job much faster?
questions.rationale: Paraphrase with almost no keyword overlap ('reduced nightly job time from 5 hours to 40 minutes').

questions.question: Who has led a migration from a monolith to microservices?
questions.rationale: Rachel led exactly this. Elena's MySQL-to-PostgreSQL migration is a database migration, not monolith-to-microservices.

questions.question: Who has introduced feature flags or trunk-based development?

relevant.contains: adoption of feature flags and trunk-based development

questions.rationale: Elena drove the adoption (experience) and spoke about it (projects). Two chunks from one candidate: tests that both surface.

questions.question: Who has worked on fraud detection?
questions.rationale: Elena's teams own fraud detection and shipped a fraud model.

questions.question: Who speaks German?
questions.rationale: Elena's Languages section. Her header mentions Berlin, which is not evidence of speaking German.

questions.question: Who knows the Go programming language?
questions.rationale: Mei (skills and a Go project) and Fatima (skills). 'Go' is a short, ambiguous token; a known weak spot for keyword search.

questions.question: Who has used gradient boosting models such as XGBoost or LightGBM?
questions.rationale: Sara used XGBoost; Omar forecasted demand with LightGBM (also gradient boosting).

questions.question: Who has managed secrets with a tool like HashiCorp Vault?
questions.rationale: Fatima rotated secrets into Vault and lists it.

questions.question: Who built a high-throughput rate limiter?
questions.rationale: Mei's project, load-tested to 5k requests/second.

questions.question: Who has worked as a teaching assistant?
questions.rationale: Sara was a TA. Hannah was a teacher, not a teaching assistant: a near-miss distractor.

negative_questions.question: Who has COBOL mainframe experience?
negative_questions.rationale: No resume mentions COBOL or mainframes.

negative_questions.question: Who is a licensed medical doctor?
Who is a certified Salesforce administrator?
